title: Block: A Prefix Sum Array
oneLiner: Answer many range-sum queries with a prefix array one longer than the input.
keyTakeaway: Make the prefix array n + 1 long with prefix[0] = 0; then the sum of nums[l..r] is prefix[r + 1] minus prefix[l], with no special case for l = 0.
explanation:
For each query [left, right] (inclusive, valid indices), return the sum of nums[left..right]. [1, 2, 3, 4] with queries [[0, 3], [1, 2]] gives [10, 5].

Build prefix once: prefix[0] = 0 and prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i], so prefix[i] is the sum of the first i elements. Each query is then one subtraction. The extra leading 0 is what removes the off-by-one.

starterCode.python:
def range_sums(nums, queries):
    # 1. Make a prefix array one longer than the input, starting with 0.
    # 2. Fill it so prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i].
    # 3. For each query [left, right], the sum is prefix[right + 1] minus prefix[left].
    # 4. Return the sums in query order.
    return []

gotchas: A prefix array of length n, which makes the l = 0 query a special case or an index error.
prefix[r] - prefix[l] instead of prefix[r + 1] - prefix[l], dropping the last element.

complexity.note: O(n) to build the prefix array, then O(1) per query for m queries.
